dedupe_keys.name: national risk assessments a cross country perspective oecd revised 2018

description: This OECD report reviews how member countries carry out national risk assessments, the all-hazards studies that map the major risks a country faces in the medium term, from natural disasters and disease outbreaks to industrial accidents and terrorist attacks. It covers the purposes and methods of national risk assessment, transparency and accountability, multi-level governance and stakeholder participation, scope, hazard and threat identification, time horizons and impact analysis, and links these to the OECD Recommendation on the Governance of Critical Risks, the EU Civil Protection Mechanism and the Sendai Framework. The OECD published it in 2017 with a revised version in October 2018. Coverage is OECD countries. Format and access: a free 308-page PDF. Licence: OECD terms, not read; free. Caveats: it compares practice and governance, not publishing national risk registers, and assessments cited may since have been updated. It helps locate and interpret the national risk registers and reasonable worst-case scenarios that set hazard assumptions for infrastructure resilience studies. A related catalogue record is the National Risk Assessment for Ireland 2023.
